Colors

A complete color system with 10 shades (50–950) for each brand color, semantic aliases, and utility classes for text, background, border, and more.

Basic Example

ZAKUIKit provides nine color scales: primary, secondary, success, warning, danger, info, and neutral. Each scale contains 11 shades from 50 (lightest) to 950 (darkest). Click any swatch to copy its hex value.

Color Variables

Every color is exposed as a CSS custom property. Use these variables directly in your CSS to stay theme-aware.

css 
/* Semantic aliases */
--zak-color-primary: var(--zak-primary-500);
--zak-color-secondary: var(--zak-secondary-500);
--zak-color-success: var(--zak-success-500);
--zak-color-warning: var(--zak-warning-500);
--zak-color-danger: var(--zak-danger-500);
--zak-color-info: var(--zak-info-500);

/* Usage */
.button-hero {
  background-color: var(--zak-color-primary);
  color: var(--zak-text-inverse);
}

Variable reference

Variable Default value Description
--zak-primary-500 #3b82f6 Primary brand color (blue)
--zak-secondary-500 #6b7280 Secondary brand color (gray)
--zak-success-500 #22c55e Success / positive state
--zak-warning-500 #f59e0b Warning / caution state
--zak-danger-500 #ef4444 Danger / error state
--zak-info-500 #06b6d4 Informational state
--zak-neutral-500 #737373 Neutral gray
--zak-text #1e293b Primary text color
--zak-text-muted #64748b Secondary text color
--zak-border #e2e8f0 Default border color
--zak-bg #ffffff Page background
--zak-surface #ffffff Card / surface background

Semantic Colors

Use semantic colors to communicate state consistently: success for positive outcomes, danger for errors, warning for cautions, and info for neutral guidance.

Contextual usage
Success — Operation completed successfully.
Error — Something went wrong. Try again.
Warning — Your session will expire soon.
Info — A software update is available.
html 
<div class="zak-border zak-border-danger">
  <strong class="zak-text-danger">Error</strong> — Something went wrong.
</div>

Color Accessibility

All ZAKUIKit color combinations have been designed to meet WCAG AA contrast requirements. When combining text and background, always verify a minimum contrast ratio of 4.5:1 for normal text and 3:1 for large text (18pt+ / 14pt bold+).

Combination Contrast ratio WCAG level Status
White text on --zak-primary-600 5.9:1 AA Pass
White text on --zak-primary-700 7.4:1 AAA Pass
Dark text on --zak-primary-100 10.2:1 AAA Pass
White text on --zak-danger-600 4.8:1 AA Pass
White text on --zak-warning-500 2.3:1 — Fail — use dark text instead
Dark text on --zak-warning-100 11.4:1 AAA Pass
--zak-text-muted on white 4.6:1 AA Pass

Best practices

  • Never rely on color alone to convey meaning — pair color with an icon, text, or label.
  • Use --zak-text-muted sparingly for secondary content only.
  • For error messages, combine color with a warning symbol and descriptive text.
  • Always support prefers-reduced-motion and provide visible focus states.

Dark Theme

Semantic color aliases automatically adjust in dark mode. For example, --zak-color-primary brightens from #3b82f6 to #60a5fa to maintain contrast on dark surfaces.

css 
[data-theme="dark"] {
  --zak-color-primary: var(--zak-primary-400);
  --zak-color-secondary: var(--zak-secondary-400);
  --zak-color-success: var(--zak-success-400);
  --zak-color-warning: var(--zak-warning-400);
  --zak-color-danger: var(--zak-danger-400);
  --zak-color-info: var(--zak-info-400);
}
